verified_summary: Pexels states photos and videos are free for commercial use.
Attribution is not required under the Pexels license summary.
The license prohibits implying endorsement by depicted people or brands and restricts standalone redistribution/sale.
records.production_implication: Provider terms can satisfy the base copyright-license gate, but asset-level person/brand/trademark/evidence-boundary review remains mandatory.

verified_summary: Unsplash states images are free for most commercial/personal projects and attribution is not required.
Unsplash explicitly distinguishes its copyright license from other rights affecting recognizable people, private property and trademarks.
Unsplash states it cannot guarantee the scope of releases for every uploaded image.
records.production_implication: Identifiable-person/property/brand assets must not be auto-whitelisted solely from the provider license; conditional or human review is required when target use could imply endorsement or company identity.

verified_summary: Pixabay states Content may be used for free and may be modified subject to prohibited uses.
Standalone redistribution is restricted and misleading/deceptive use is prohibited.
Pixabay notes that trademarks, personality/privacy, property and other rights may require separate consent and are the user's responsibility.
records.production_implication: Base provider license is necessary but not sufficient for commercial Production approval; third-party rights and misleading-use gates remain mandatory.

cross_provider_conclusion: all three providers can be considered free-first candidate sources under their current published terms
none should be treated as a universal asset whitelist
commercial website use can still be unsafe for a specific asset/use because depicted people, brands, property or misleading context can add separate rights/consent constraints
license evidence must be rechecked on trigger; this registry is not permanent legal clearance
